## Initiated Ordinance 309 (Slaughterhouse Ban)

Nearly two-thirds (64.6%) opposed the slaughterhouse ban Denver's Initiated Ordinance 309 in the November 5, 2024 election. Denver voters elected to keep the city's only slaughterhouse open, a blow for the organizers of Ordinance 309.

Initiated Ordinance 309 would prohibit the construction, maintenance or use of slaughterhouses within Denver city limits starting in January 2026. Superior Farms, a lamb processing plant, is Denver's only slaughterhouse, making it the sole facility that would be directly impacted by the ballot measure.

## Initiated Ordinance 308 (Fur Ban)

Denver voters rejected Initiated Ordinance 308, which would have banned the sale of new fur products in the city. According to the most recent data from the city's election division, about 58% of voters opposed the measure.

The measure was brought forward by a grassroots group called Pro-Animal Future, who also placed Ordinance 308, a proposed ban on the sale of fur, on Denver's ballot.

Both measures were decisively rejected by Denver voters in November 2024.

DC's fullservice restaurant segment lost 900 jobs between March 2025 and June 2025, representing a 2.8% decline in fullservice restaurant jobs. Restaurant operators adjusted their business models to prepare for the scheduled July 1 increase in the minimum tipped wage from $10 to $12.
